content.text: {"answer": "At most three upkeep runs can start per repository for one event (FR12.19a, added 2026-10-25). Pull requests are picked by how long ago they were last upkept, longest ago first. A pull request that has never been upkept goes first. Next comes the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest, then the one after that, and so on. Picking the oldest pull request first without this ordering kept choosing the same three failing PRs on every push, and every other loop PR was deferred indefinitely. The pull requests that don't get a run are left for the next event. For example, with 5 PRs behind main, the 3 oldest start and 14 and 15 wait. In another example, 14 and 15 start, then 12, because 11, 12 and 13 were each upkept at the last push and 12 was upkept earliest.", "sources": ["specs/external-floor/spec.md", "apps/stations/src/events/loop-upkeep-handlers.ts", "apps/stations/src/events/loop-upkeep-handlers.test.ts", "libs/shared/src/work/backlog/loop-pr-upkeep.ts"]}
